correctness.rationale: The 0-Hecke normal forms and descending-input thresholds establish exactly n! distinct transformations. Packing at most m-1 binary cuts per m-level probe gives the constructive upper bound. Comparing the longest sorting element with its n-1 distinct adjacent coatoms proves every input distinguishes at most m-1 of these pairs and yields a matching lower bound. Every boundary n,m>=2 and the trivial n=1/m=1 cases is covered; finite check scripts corroborate nine small parameter pairs.

value.rationale: A motivated all-parameter nonadaptive system-identification invariant with a sharp and constructive alphabet/query tradeoff; distinct top coatoms yield a structural optimality obstruction. This quantifies exactly how many parallel observable inputs are required to identify any comparator transformation, not a trivial restatement of n! size or monoid faithfulness.
